source: Real pi session log `2026-11-18T22-02-48-983Z_01a1f0af-1716-…jsonl` (52 entries), the session this repo's browser client was attached to while the panel/pairing work was being done. Built by `capture.py` in this directory — run it against that log to regenerate the input. Entries are verbatim (ids, parentIds, timestamps, types, roles, tool names, mimeTypes); content is length-marked `«N»`, and everything under `details` is marked regardless of length, because a pairing token in a fixture is a credential in a repository.
extensionVersion: @geohar/un-bien 0.25.15 (the build installed in this pi). The repo's extension source is at 0.25.11, and npm carries 0.25.13/14/15 that have no commits or tags in this repository — see vocab.md, 'Which build produced this', for why that does not invalidate the fixture.
scrub: Content → `«length»`; `details.*` → `«length»` at any length (tokens, URIs); strings longer than 48 chars truncated to the projection's readable cap. Structure, ids, parentIds, timestamps, tool names, mimeTypes verbatim.
description: The first scenario that exercises the DURABLE plane: three `get_entries` response pages (two non-empty, then the empty terminal page carrying the active-leaf beacon) instead of live frames. Until now every scenario fed live frames, so entry folding — `SessionState+BirthEntry` on one side, `applyEntries`/the tree on the other — was compared by NO corpus, on either side. That gap is how a duplicate-row bug survived here: the live path keyed custom notices `cust<hash>` and the durable path keyed them `notice<hash>`, and no fixture reached that code. This one does: it carries 3 `custom_message` entries (two `display:false` bookkeeping, one `un-bien:pair-code` with details), 15 pi-internal `custom` entries (indexed, never rendered), message/toolResult entries, and a real session root.
note: The PAGE FRAMING is authored, not observed: pi pages by its own byte budget and no capture contains a `get_entries` response (0 in all 18 scenarios — the client sends that request itself, so it never appeared in the broadcast stream the frame captures recorded). The framing follows the rule both folds already implement and agree on — a non-empty page's `leafId` is only a resume cursor, and the active-leaf beacon is the `leafId` of the page that came back EMPTY (`EnvelopeReducer.swift:145-159`, `web-client/src/reducer.ts:571-587`). Page boundaries at 30/22 entries are arbitrary; a fold that changes its mind about rows because a page broke at a different entry is the kind of thing this scenario should catch, so keep the boundaries and say so.
